description:
Execute a plan for a single shard. Writes only; deletion is the next ticket.

Scan the shard prefix by name and size — an interval already holding a single object needs no work. For each planned pack: read its constituents, concatenate their transaction payloads in version order, and put the result at the pack's max-named key. That key is the one its newest constituent already occupies, because a chunk is named for the max version it contains and a pack's max is its newest constituent's max. So a pack write is an overwrite, using put/4 rather than put_if_not_exists/4. Set the consolidation level in the header flags.

Checks:

- Before the put, assert the pack's data section equals the byte concatenation of its constituents' data sections. Cheap, and it catches a mis-assembled pack before it is durable.
- Primary test: for any target version, ChunkReader.read_from_version/3 yields an identical sequence of {version, data} tuples before and after. This is the exit criterion of the whole epic, expressed as an exact equality rather than a "nothing was lost" check.

Ship as a mix task. Placement, scheduling and supervision are deliberately deferred to a later ticket so this can be validated by hand against real data first.

Note for rollout: packs written without deletion sit alongside their constituents, so reads fetch both and discard the overlap. That is a temporary read regression by design. Gate this to staging or behind a flag until deletion lands.
title: Consolidator: write packs for one shard (no deletion)
